articles.title: China eleva tarifa sobre carne brasileira a 67% após fim da cota | G1
articles.standfirst: Brasil atingiu o limite de 1,106 milhão de toneladas sem sobretaxa em 2026. Para o próximo ano, frigoríficos já planejam antecipar abates e embarques diante da expectativa de esgotar a nova cota em até três meses.
articles.summary: Brasil atingiu o limite de 1,106 milhão de toneladas sem sobretaxa em 2026. Para o próximo ano, frigoríficos já planejam antecipar abates e embarques.
articles.body:
O presidente do Brasil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, cumprimentam-se cerimônia no Palácio do Povo, em Pequim, no dia 13 de maio de 2025 — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert/Presidência da República

A partir desta quinta-feira (1º), a carne brasileira passa a pagar uma tarifa adicional de 55% para entrar no mercado chinês. Somada ao imposto de 12% que já era aplicado, a cobrança total chega a 67%.

O aumento ocorre porque o Brasil esgotou, na quarta-feira (30), a cota de vendas sem a sobretaxa para a China, maior compradora da carne bovina brasileira.

➡️ O governo chinês anunciou a tarifa adicional para vários países no fim de 2025 para proteger os seus produtores locais. Segundo as autoridades do país, eles vinham sendo prejudicados pela importação de carne mais barata.

Neste ano, a cota brasileira de vendas sem sobretaxa foi de 1,106 milhão de toneladas . Em 2027, o limite sobe para 1,128 milhão de toneladas , mas deve ser esgotado bem mais cedo , segundo o presidente da Associação Brasileira das Indústrias Exportadoras de Carnes (Abiec), Roberto Perosa.

“Se for o que estamos esperando, pode haver final da cota em março, mais tardar em abril, o que é muito ruim para todo o setor. Sairemos de três meses de sufoco para seis”, disse ele, em setembro.

A diferença de 2027 em relação a este ano é que o setor pode se preparar com antecedência e acelerar os embarques . A cota deste ano, por exemplo, foi anunciada só no fim de 2025, o que deixou pouco tempo para pecuaristas e frigoríficos se organizarem.

Agora, como eles já sabem quanto poderão vender sem sobretaxa, vão disputar espaço na cota antes mesmo de ela entrar em vigor.

Isso, na verdade, já vem acontecendo. A previsão do setor é que os abates comecem neste mês e os embarques, em novembro, para que a carne chegue à China em janeiro de 2027. A viagem de navio do Brasil à China leva de 40 a 45 dias.

Se as vendas se concentrarem no início de 2027, a tendência é que os negócios entre os dois países percam ritmo no restante do ano. Mas tudo depende também do apetite chinês. Segundo Perosa, os estoques de carne bovina no país estão elevados, assim como a produção de carne suína.

Ou seja, os frigoríficos podem se antecipar para vender, mas ainda não sabem em que ritmo os chineses vão comprar.

A cota do Brasil só foi oficialmente atingida no fim de setembro, mas as exportações começaram a perder ritmo dois meses antes, disse Perosa, que classificou julho, agosto e setembro como meses “duríssimos” para a indústria.

Nesse período, as exportações continuaram em volumes menores para cumprir contratos pontuais já firmados. Com menos vendas para o principal cliente, os frigoríficos precisaram redirecionar a carne para outros mercados e viram suas margens de lucro diminuir.

A queda nas vendas também aperta o caixa dos frigoríficos, já que parte deles usa os pagamentos antecipados dos compradores chineses para cobrir as despesas do dia a dia. Com menos negócios, entra menos dinheiro para manter as operações.

No final de setembro, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva afirmou que o Uruguai havia cedido ao Brasil parte da cota de exportação de carne bovina à China . No entanto, o Ministério do Comércio da China não se pronunciou publicamente sobre os pedidos brasileiros.

Para evitar que a cota acabe tão cedo e distribuir melhor as vendas ao longo de 2027, a Abiec voltou a discutir com o governo uma divisão do volume entre os frigoríficos. Cada empresa teria uma parte, definida por critérios como sua participação nas exportações e seu histórico de vendas.

Segundo Perosa, a entidade tentou viabilizar uma proposta semelhante para 2026, mas o governo decidiu não fazer a divisão. Agora, a discussão ganha força com a entrada de mais frigoríficos brasileiros no mercado chinês, o que aumenta a disputa pela mesma cota.

Na última terça-feira (29), por exemplo, a China autorizou mais duas unidades a vender carne bovina ao país: a Supremo Carnes , de Carlos Chagas (MG), e a Masterboi , de Canhotinho (PE), segundo comunicado do Ministério da Agricultura .

A China também autorizou duas unidades de carne de frango: a Avivar Alimentos, de São Sebastião do Oeste (MG), e a Cooperativa Dália Alimentos, de Arroio do Meio (RS).

articles.title: Oil prices stay flat as markets weigh US-Iran talks and Middle East supply
articles.summary: Oil prices showed little movement in early trading on Thursday after both major benchmarks gained about $1 a barrel in the previous session.
articles.body: Oil prices showed little movement in early trading on Thursday after both major benchmarks gained about $1 a barrel in the previous session. The oil market remained calm as investors weighed developments in US-Iran peace talks and the recovery in Middle East crude exports.Around 7 am IST, WTI Crude was trading at $90.16 a barrel, down 26 cents, or 0.29%, while Brent Crude stood at $97.93 a barrel, lower by 10 cents, or 0.10%.The largely flat session came after a strong September for oil prices. Brent has gained around 14% this month, marking its biggest monthly rise since July. WTI, meanwhile, has advanced about 5% over the month.Markets are also assessing the outlook for crude supplies from the Middle East as they track the latest developments around US-Iran peace talks. The movement in prices remained limited in early Thursday trading despite the gains recorded by both benchmarks in the previous session.The direction of WTI could depend on developments around the US-Iran negotiations. A new catalyst, such as progress in peace negotiations, will be needed for WTI to break below the immediate support level of $88 a barrel, he added.Qatar on Tuesday said that it hoped shuttle diplomacy between Tehran and Washington could result in a breakthrough. The comments came as uncertainty continued around the possibility of a deal between the two countries.US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, denied reports from Axios and CNN that cited US officials as saying he was prepared to offer Iran sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds in exchange for "concrete" steps from Tehran on its nuclear programme.The oil market is also tracking the pace at which supplies from the region are returning. Saudi Arabia resumed oil tanker loadings from Yanbu on Tuesday after restarting its East-West Pipeline.Gulf exports have also recovered, according to Goldman Sachs. The bank estimated that Gulf oil exports, including "dark exports" involving ships operating with their location transponders turned off, had reached 23.3 million barrels per day over the last week. That is in line with the 2025 average, while exports doubled in September, Goldman Sachs said in a note on Tuesday.Production policy is another factor in focus ahead of the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday. Two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters that OPEC+ oil-producing countries are likely to leave their November oil production targets unchanged.US inventory data offered a mixed picture for the market. Crude stocks increased by 922,000 barrels to 427.3 million barrels in the week ended September 25, the Energy Information Administration said. articles.title: LPG price hike: 19-kg commercial cylinder gets Rs 62.50 costlier; new Aadhaar rule kicks in for domestic users
articles.summary: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1, taking the price to Rs 2,810.
articles.body: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1, taking the price to Rs 2,810. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137 per litre.The changes come as domestic LPG consumers face a new requirement from October 1, 2026. Those seeking to book refills at the regulated Retail Selling Price (RSP) with applicable subsidy will now need to have completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA).The authentication requirement is aimed at ensuring that subsidised LPG reaches genuine and deserving households. Each LPG connection is linked to an Aadhaar-authenticated consumer to prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use, remove duplicate and ineligible connections, and make subsidy delivery more targeted and transparent.Consumers who have already completed BAA will not need to repeat the process and can continue booking refills as before. Those who have not completed it will be able to book a refill at the RSP with subsidy once their authentication is completed.Consumers can complete the authentication process through several channels. During refill delivery, the delivery person can carry out BAA on the spot using the OMC mobile application.The process can also be completed by visiting the LPG distributor's showroom. Consumers can alternatively complete it themselves from home through their OMC's mobile application: IndianOil ONE for Indane customers, HelloBPCL for Bharatgas customers and HP PAY for HP Gas customers.Consumers who are unwilling or unable to complete BAA can still receive LPG. They will have to register their choice through their OMC's digital channels, including the consumer web portal, mobile app, WhatsApp chatbot, IVRS or other available channels.In such cases, LPG will be supplied at the applicable market price without subsidy, in 5-kg or 10-kg cylinders, subject to local availability with the OMC.Consumers who have not yet completed BAA have been urged to do so through any of the available channels, which are accessible in both urban and rural areas.You use AI every day. articles.title: September pain on Dalal Street: FPIs pull out 46k crore from equities
articles.summary: For the first time in two years, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned net sellers across all reported equity and debt segments in September.
articles.body: For the first time in two years, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) turned net sellers across all reported equity and debt segments in September.Also, on a standalone basis, FPIs were net sellers at Rs 35,861 crore in stocks till Sept 29. They net sold another Rs 10,148 crore worth of stocks on Sept 30, taking the month’s total figures to about Rs 46,000 crore, data from NSDL and BSE showed.The net selling figures for Sept in stocks came after two consecutive months of net buying: Rs 29,631 crore in Aug and Rs 20,200 crore in July. For the current year, net selling by FPIs at Rs 2.6 lakh crore is already way ahead of the previous year’s Rs 1.7 lakh crore net outflow by this influential investor group. The 2026 outflow is now the highest ever yearly net selling figure, NSDL data showed.Latest data showed that in addition to equities, FPIs were sellers in debt (general limit) at Rs 5,247 crore, in debt (VRR or Voluntary Retention Route) at Rs 5,049 crore, in debt (FAR or Fully Accessible Route) at Rs 10,431 crore and in hybrid at Rs 2,078 crore.FPIs were, however, net buyers in three of the five mutual fund segments: Rs 247 crore in equities, Rs 1 crore in debt and Rs 99 crore in hybrid, while they were net sellers in funds categorised under ‘other’ heads and didn’t put in any money in solutions-oriented schemes, NSDL data showed.The strong selling by FPIs in the current market came even as the rupee weakened, the price of crude oil—the single biggest import item for India—rose sharply to above the $115/barrel level for the Indian basket, and sensex and Nifty both lost about 6% each.
